title: Protocol 01: Antenatal Care (ANC) Guidelines for Frontline Health Workers
full_markdown:
# Protocol 01: Antenatal Care (ANC) Guidelines for Frontline Health Workers

Disclaimer: Educational and operational decision support for trained frontline health workers. Protocols are simplified hackathon materials and are not for clinical use. This system does not replace clinical judgment or qualified medical care.

---

### ANC-1.1: Registration and First ANC Visit
- Every pregnant woman must be registered as early as pregnancy is suspected or confirmed, ideally within the first 12 weeks (first trimester) from the Last Menstrual Period (LMP).
- Issue the Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card immediately upon registration.
- Record baseline weight, blood pressure, hemoglobin (Hb), urine albumin/sugar, and blood grouping.
- Calculate Expected Date of Delivery (EDD) = LMP + 9 months + 7 days (or 280 days).

### ANC-1.2: ANC Visit Schedule
A minimum of four comprehensive antenatal visits are mandated under national guidelines:
1. First ANC Visit: Within 12 weeks of pregnancy (first trimester).
2. Second ANC Visit: Between 14 and 26 weeks of pregnancy (second trimester).
3. Third ANC Visit: Between 28 and 34 weeks of pregnancy (third trimester).
4. Fourth ANC Visit: Between 36 weeks and delivery/term.
- Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA): Organized on the 9th of every month at designated health facilities for specialist check-ups and ultrasound screening.

### ANC-1.3: Td Immunisation in Pregnancy
- Tetanus and adult Diphtheria (Td) vaccine replaces the older TT vaccine.
- Td-1: Administer as early in pregnancy as possible.
- Td-2: Administer 4 weeks (28 days) after Td-1.
- Td Booster: If the pregnant woman received 2 doses of Td/TT in a pregnancy within the previous 3 years, only one Td booster dose is required in the current pregnancy.
- Route and dose: 0.5 ml intramuscularly (IM) in the upper arm (deltoid).

### ANC-1.4: Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) and Calcium Supplementation
- Folic Acid: 1 tablet (400 mcg folic acid) daily during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks) to prevent neural tube defects.
- Iron and Folic Acid (IFA): 1 tablet (100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid) daily starting from the 14th week of pregnancy (second trimester) for a minimum of 180 days during pregnancy and continuing for 180 days postpartum.
- In severe anaemia (Hb < 7 g/dL), double IFA dose or refer immediately.
- Calcium Supplementation: Two 500 mg elemental calcium tablets daily (total 1000 mg) starting from 14 weeks onwards until 6 months postpartum.
- Important counseling: IFA and Calcium tablets must NEVER be swallowed together; take Calcium with meals and IFA at bedtime or between meals with lemon water or plain water. Avoid taking IFA with milk, tea, or coffee.

### ANC-1.5: High-Risk Pregnancy (HRP) Identification
Any pregnant woman with one or more of the following conditions is classified as High-Risk Pregnancy:
- Severe anaemia: Hemoglobin < 7 g/dL.
- Hypertension: Systolic BP >= 140 mmHg and/or Diastolic BP >= 90 mmHg.
- Age: Below 18 years or above 35 years.
- Short stature: Height < 140 cm.
- Previous obstetric complications: Previous Caesarean section, stillbirth, recurrent abortion, postpartum haemorrhage (PPH).
- Multiple gestation: Twin or triplet pregnancy.
- Medical disorders: Pre-existing or gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), heart disease, kidney disease, HIV/TB positive.
- Action: Flag MCP card with red sticker, notify ANM/Medical Officer, schedule home follow-up visits every 14 days, and arrange institutional delivery at Chandrapuri District Hospital.

### ANC-1.6: Birth Preparedness and Complication Readiness
- Identify delivery facility: Nearest 24x7 Functional Primary Health Centre (PHC) or Chandrapuri District Hospital.
- Arrange emergency transport: Save contact numbers for 108 (Emergency Ambulance) and 102 (Janani Express).
- Identify two potential blood donors with compatible blood group.
- Save funds for delivery-related out-of-pocket expenses.
- Prepare clean delivery kit and newborn essentials (two clean dry towels, warm clothes, cord ties).

title: Protocol 02: Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) Guidelines
full_markdown:
# Protocol 02: Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) Guidelines

Disclaimer: Educational and operational decision support for trained frontline health workers. Protocols are simplified hackathon materials and are not for clinical use. This system does not replace clinical judgment or qualified medical care.

---

### IMM-1.1: Birth Doses (Within 24 Hours of Birth)
- BCG: 0.05 ml (if given <1 month age; 0.1 ml if given after 1 month) intradermal (ID) on left upper arm. Protects against childhood tuberculosis.
- OPV-0: 2 drops orally.
- Hepatitis B Birth Dose: 0.5 ml intramuscular (IM) on anterolateral aspect of mid-thigh. Must be administered within 24 hours of birth to prevent mother-to-child transmission.

### IMM-1.2: Six Weeks Immunisation
- OPV-1: 2 drops orally.
- Pentavalent-1 (DPT + Hep B + Hib): 0.5 ml IM, anterolateral aspect of mid-thigh.
- Rotavirus-1 (RVV): 5 drops orally (or 2.5 ml depending on presentation). Protects against rotavirus diarrhoea.
- fIPV-1 (Fractional Inactivated Polio Vaccine): 0.1 ml ID on right upper arm.
- PCV-1 (Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine): 0.5 ml IM on anterolateral mid-thigh.

### IMM-1.3: Ten Weeks Immunisation
- OPV-2: 2 drops orally.
- Pentavalent-2: 0.5 ml IM on anterolateral mid-thigh.
- Rotavirus-2: 5 drops orally.

### IMM-1.4: Fourteen Weeks Immunisation
- OPV-3: 2 drops orally.
- Pentavalent-3: 0.5 ml IM on anterolateral mid-thigh.
- Rotavirus-3: 5 drops orally.
- fIPV-2: 0.1 ml ID on right upper arm.
- PCV-2: 0.5 ml IM on anterolateral mid-thigh.

### IMM-1.5: Nine to Twelve Months Immunisation
- Measles-Rubella (MR) 1st Dose: 0.5 ml subcutaneous (SC) on right upper arm. Administer at completion of 9 months (270 days).
- JE-1 (Japanese Encephalitis): 0.5 ml SC on left upper arm in endemic districts.
- PCV Booster: 0.5 ml IM on anterolateral mid-thigh.
- Vitamin A 1st Dose: 1 ml (100,000 International Units) orally with spoon.

### IMM-1.6: Sixteen to Twenty-Four Months Immunisation
- MR 2nd Dose: 0.5 ml SC on right upper arm.
- DPT Booster 1: 0.5 ml IM on anterolateral mid-thigh.
- OPV Booster: 2 drops orally.
- JE-2: 0.5 ml SC on left upper arm in endemic districts.
- Vitamin A 2nd Dose: 2 ml (200,000 IU) orally; subsequent doses given every 6 months up to 5 years (total 9 doses).

### IMM-1.7: Five to Six Years Immunisation
- DPT Booster 2: 0.5 ml IM in upper arm (deltoid). Strengthens immunity against Diphtheria, Pertussis, and Tetanus.

### IMM-1.8: School Age (Ten and Sixteen Years)
- Td at 10 Years: 0.5 ml IM in upper arm (deltoid).
- Td at 16 Years: 0.5 ml IM in upper arm (deltoid).

### IMM-1.9: Cold Chain and Adverse Events Following Immunisation (AEFI)
- Vaccine Storage: Store all vaccines between +2°C and +8°C in Ice-Lined Refrigerators (ILR) or conditioned vaccine carriers.
- Never freeze freeze-sensitive vaccines (Pentavalent, Td, PCV, Hep B).
- Minor AEFI: Mild fever and injection site swelling are normal; counsel parents to give paracetamol drops/syrup and cold water compress.
- Serious AEFI (Anaphylaxis, persistent scream, seizures): Maintain airway, give injection adrenaline if trained/ANM available, and refer urgently to Chandrapuri District Hospital.

title: Protocol 03: Emergency Signs and Immediate Referral (ESC)
full_markdown:
# Protocol 03: Emergency Signs and Immediate Referral (ESC)

Disclaimer: Educational and operational decision support for trained frontline health workers. Protocols are simplified hackathon materials and are not for clinical use. This system does not replace clinical judgment or qualified medical care.

---

### ESC-1.1: Maternal Danger Signs During Pregnancy
Any of the following signs during pregnancy constitutes an obstetric emergency requiring immediate referral to Chandrapuri District Hospital:
- Vaginal bleeding (spotting, fresh bleeding, clots, or placenta praevia suspicion).
- Severe headache with blurred vision, seeing spots, or epigastric pain (signs of impending eclampsia).
- Convulsions, fits, or loss of consciousness (eclampsia).
- High blood pressure (Systolic BP >= 160 mmHg or Diastolic BP >= 110 mmHg, or >= 140/90 mmHg with symptoms).
- High fever (temperature > 101°F / 38.3°C) with chills or rigors.
- Severe continuous abdominal pain or rigid abdomen.
- Reduced or absent fetal movements after 24 weeks / 5th month of gestation.
- Foul-smelling vaginal discharge.
- Severe breathlessness, difficulty breathing, or severe paleness of tongue/palms (severe anaemia).

### ESC-1.2: Maternal Danger Signs During Labour and Delivery
Immediate emergency referral is required when any of the following occur:
- Prolonged labour: Labour pains lasting longer than 12 hours without progress.
- Premature or prolonged rupture of membranes (PROM): Water breaks more than 18 hours before delivery or foul-smelling amniotic fluid.
- Cord prolapse: Umbilical cord visible or protruding from the vagina (place mother in knee-chest position immediately).
- Abnormal presentation: Hand, foot, or breech presenting first instead of head.
- Retained placenta: Placenta not delivered within 30 minutes after baby's birth.
- Severe vaginal bleeding during or immediately following labour.
- Fits, convulsions, or maternal collapse during delivery.

### ESC-1.3: Maternal Postpartum Danger Signs (After Delivery)
During the 42 days following delivery, watch for:
- Severe Postpartum Haemorrhage (PPH): Bleeding that soaks more than two sanitary pads in one hour, or sudden large gush of blood.
- High fever (>101°F / 38.3°C) with chills, shivering, or foul-smelling lochia (puerperal sepsis).
- Severe, unbearable lower abdominal pain.
- Fits, seizures, or loss of consciousness.
- Severe unilateral calf pain, swollen red calf, or sudden chest pain with breathlessness (deep vein thrombosis / pulmonary embolism).
- Severe postnatal depression, agitation, delusions, suicidal thoughts, or wanting to harm the infant (postpartum psychosis).

### ESC-2.1: Newborn and Young Infant Danger Signs (Birth to 2 Months)
A young infant with ANY of the following signs must be referred IMMEDIATELY to Chandrapuri District Hospital Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU):
- Inability to feed or breastfeed, or stopping feeding completely.
- Convulsions, fits, or abnormal twitching.
- Fast breathing: Breathing rate 60 breaths per minute or faster.
- Severe chest indrawing (lower chest wall goes deep in when baby breathes in).
- High fever (axillary temperature >= 37.5°C / 99.5°F) or hypothermia (body feels cold, temperature < 35.5°C / 95.9°F).
- Lethargy, floppiness, unusually difficult to wake, or unconsciousness.
- Yellow palms and soles, or deep jaundice appearing in first 24 hours of life.
- Umbilical redness spreading to surrounding abdominal skin, or draining foul pus.
- Numerous skin pustules or large bullae/blisters.
- Continuous grunting or wheezing while breathing.

### ESC-2.2: Child Danger Signs (2 Months to 5 Years)
Any child presenting with General Danger Signs must be referred urgently to the nearest First Referral Unit (FRU) / Chandrapuri District Hospital:
- Inability to drink, breastfeed, or take any oral fluids.
- Vomits everything (cannot keep anything down).
- Convulsions or seizures during the current illness.
- Lethargic, abnormally sleepy, or unconscious.
- Stridor in a calm child (harsh rasping sound on breathing in).
- Severe acute malnutrition with bilateral pitting edema of both feet.
- Extremely pale conjunctiva, palms, or tongue (life-threatening anaemia).
- Stiff neck with high fever (suspected meningitis).

### ESC-2.3: Immediate Referral Actions and Transport Protocols
When an emergency danger sign is identified:
1. Explain urgency calmly to the family; do not delay departure.
2. Call 108 Emergency Ambulance or 102 Janani Express immediately.
3. Keep the patient warm (wrap baby with warm cloth / Kangaroo Mother Care; cover mother).
4. If convulsions or vomiting occur: Turn patient on their side to prevent choking and aspiration; clear airway; NEVER put spoon or fingers in mouth; NEVER give fluids orally.
5. In cord prolapse: Keep woman in knee-chest or elevated pelvis position with sterile cloth supporting cord; do not push cord back inside.
6. Carry MCP card, referral slip with recorded vitals and time of onset, and accompany the patient to Chandrapuri District Hospital.

title: Protocol 04: Home-Based Newborn Care (HBNC) Guidelines
full_markdown:
# Protocol 04: Home-Based Newborn Care (HBNC) Guidelines

Disclaimer: Educational and operational decision support for trained frontline health workers. Protocols are simplified hackathon materials and are not for clinical use. This system does not replace clinical judgment or qualified medical care.

---

### HBNC-1.1: Institutional Delivery Home Visit Schedule
For babies born in health institutions (hospital, CHC, PHC), the ASHA must conduct 6 mandatory home visits:
- Visit 1: Day 3 of life.
- Visit 2: Day 7 of life.
- Visit 3: Day 14 of life.
- Visit 4: Day 21 of life.
- Visit 5: Day 28 of life.
- Visit 6: Day 42 of life (6 weeks).

### HBNC-1.2: Home Delivery Visit Schedule
For babies delivered at home, the ASHA must conduct 7 mandatory home visits (an extra Day 1 visit):
- Visit 1: Day 1 of life (within 24 hours of birth).
- Visit 2: Day 3 of life.
- Visit 3: Day 7 of life.
- Visit 4: Day 14 of life.
- Visit 5: Day 21 of life.
- Visit 6: Day 28 of life.
- Visit 7: Day 42 of life.

### HBNC-1.3: Immediate Care at Birth and Thermal Protection
- Immediate drying: Dry baby with clean warm towel within 5 seconds of birth; remove wet towel and wrap in second warm, dry cloth.
- Delayed cord clamping: Wait 1 to 3 minutes before cutting cord to boost infant iron stores.
- Skin-to-Skin contact: Place naked baby on mother's bare chest immediately after birth.
- Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC): For Low Birth Weight (LBW) babies weighing less than 2,500g. Provide continuous skin-to-skin contact for at least 1-2 hours per session, combined with frequent exclusive breastfeeding.
- Bathing guidelines: Delay bathing for at least 48 hours for normal weight babies; delay for 7 days or until baby reaches 2.5 kg for LBW babies to prevent fatal hypothermia.

### HBNC-1.4: Exclusive Breastfeeding Initiation and Counseling
- Early initiation: Initiate breastfeeding within 1 hour of birth for all babies.
- Colostrum: First yellow thick milk is rich in protective antibodies (first natural vaccine); never discard colostrum.
- Strictly no pre-lacteal feeds: No honey, ghutti, animal milk, plain water, or sugar water.
- Exclusive breastfeeding: Only breast milk (no water or other liquids/foods) for the first 6 months of life (180 days).
- Feed on demand: At least 8 to 12 times in 24 hours, day and night.

### HBNC-1.5: Cord Care and Eye Care
- Umbilical Cord: Keep the stump clean and dry. Leave open to air.
- Do NOT apply cow dung, ash, mustard oil, ghee, kajal, or talcum powder to the umbilical stump.
- Chlorhexidine 7.1% (delivering 4% free chlorhexidine) solution/gel should be applied once daily to the umbilical stump for the first 7 days if recommended by local health department.
- Eye care: Clean eyes from inner to outer canthus with boiled cooled cotton swab; do not apply surma or kajal.

title: Protocol 05: Malnutrition Screening and Management Guidelines (NUT)
full_markdown:
# Protocol 05: Malnutrition Screening and Management Guidelines (NUT)

Disclaimer: Educational and operational decision support for trained frontline health workers. Protocols are simplified hackathon materials and are not for clinical use. This system does not replace clinical judgment or qualified medical care.

---

### NUT-1.1: Anthropometric Assessment
- Weight-for-Age: Plotted on WHO growth charts (Green = Normal, Yellow = Moderately Underweight, Red = Severely Underweight).
- Height/Length-for-Age: Measures stunting (chronic malnutrition).
- Weight-for-Height/Length: Measures wasting (acute malnutrition). A standard deviation score below -3 SD denotes Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM).

### NUT-1.2: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) Screening for 6 to 59 Months
MUAC tape is used on the left arm midway between the tip of the shoulder (acromion) and tip of the elbow (olecranon):
- Red Zone (< 11.5 cm / 115 mm): Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM). Immediate referral or community management protocol required.
- Yellow Zone (11.5 cm to 12.4 cm / 115 to 124 mm): Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM). Targeted supplemental nutrition and bi-weekly counseling.
- Green Zone (>= 12.5 cm / 125 mm): Normal nutritional status. Routine growth monitoring.
- Frequency: Monthly MUAC screening for SAM/MAM children; quarterly screening for all children aged 6 to 59 months.

### NUT-1.3: Bilateral Pitting Edema Assessment
- Press both thumbs firmly but gently on the top of both feet (dorsum of feet) for 3 seconds, then release.
- If a pit/indentation remains on both feet simultaneously, bilateral pitting edema is present.
- Bilateral pitting edema indicates Kwashiorkor (severe acute malnutrition) regardless of MUAC measurement, requiring urgent referral.

### NUT-1.4: Nutritional Rehabilitation Centre (NRC) Referral Criteria
A child aged 6-59 months must be referred to the Chandrapuri NRC under the following conditions:
1. SAM with medical complications (fever, hypothermia, pneumonia, severe diarrhoea, vomiting).
2. SAM with failed Appetite Test (unable or unwilling to eat Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food / energy-dense paste).
3. SAM with bilateral pitting edema (Grade +++ or generalized edema).
4. Any infant under 6 months of age with severe wasting or unable to breastfeed.
- Treatment at NRC includes stabilized therapeutic feeds (F-75, F-100), medical care, micronutrient supplementation, and sensory stimulation.

### NUT-1.5: Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) & Complementary Feeding
- At 6 completed months (180 days), breast milk alone is no longer sufficient; introduce semi-solid mashed complementary food.
- Frequency: 2-3 meals daily at 6-8 months; 3-4 meals daily at 9-23 months, plus 1-2 nutritious snacks (banana, boiled egg, roasted gram, khichdi enriched with oil/ghee).
- Consistency: Thick porridge/khichdi that does not drip easily from the spoon.
- Continue frequent, on-demand breastfeeding until at least 2 years of age or beyond.

sections.title: Anthropometric Assessment
sections.content:
- Weight-for-Age: Plotted on WHO growth charts (Green = Normal, Yellow = Moderately Underweight, Red = Severely Underweight).
- Height/Length-for-Age: Measures stunting (chronic malnutrition).
- Weight-for-Height/Length: Measures wasting (acute malnutrition). A standard deviation score below -3 SD denotes Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM).

sections.title: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) Screening for 6 to 59 Months
sections.content:
MUAC tape is used on the left arm midway between the tip of the shoulder (acromion) and tip of the elbow (olecranon):
- Red Zone (< 11.5 cm / 115 mm): Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM). Immediate referral or community management protocol required.
- Yellow Zone (11.5 cm to 12.4 cm / 115 to 124 mm): Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM). Targeted supplemental nutrition and bi-weekly counseling.
- Green Zone (>= 12.5 cm / 125 mm): Normal nutritional status. Routine growth monitoring.
- Frequency: Monthly MUAC screening for SAM/MAM children; quarterly screening for all children aged 6 to 59 months.

sections.title: Bilateral Pitting Edema Assessment
sections.content:
- Press both thumbs firmly but gently on the top of both feet (dorsum of feet) for 3 seconds, then release.
- If a pit/indentation remains on both feet simultaneously, bilateral pitting edema is present.
- Bilateral pitting edema indicates Kwashiorkor (severe acute malnutrition) regardless of MUAC measurement, requiring urgent referral.

sections.title: Nutritional Rehabilitation Centre (NRC) Referral Criteria
sections.content:
A child aged 6-59 months must be referred to the Chandrapuri NRC under the following conditions:
1. SAM with medical complications (fever, hypothermia, pneumonia, severe diarrhoea, vomiting).
2. SAM with failed Appetite Test (unable or unwilling to eat Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food / energy-dense paste).
3. SAM with bilateral pitting edema (Grade +++ or generalized edema).
4. Any infant under 6 months of age with severe wasting or unable to breastfeed.
- Treatment at NRC includes stabilized therapeutic feeds (F-75, F-100), medical care, micronutrient supplementation, and sensory stimulation.

title: Protocol 06: Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) Screening & Follow-Up
full_markdown:
# Protocol 06: Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) Screening & Follow-Up

Disclaimer: Educational and operational decision support for trained frontline health workers. Protocols are simplified hackathon materials and are not for clinical use. This system does not replace clinical judgment or qualified medical care.

---

### NCD-1.1: Population-Based Screening (CBAC Checklist)
- Every adult aged 30 years and older must be screened annually using the Community-Based Assessment Checklist (CBAC).
- Screening covers hypertension, diabetes mellitus, oral cancer, breast cancer, and cervical cancer.
- Suspected individuals with high CBAC risk scores (>= 4) must be referred to the Primary Health Centre / Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Sub Health Centre).

### NCD-1.2: Hypertension Cut-offs and Follow-Up Protocols
Blood pressure measurement on seated individual after 5 minutes of rest:
- Normal: Systolic BP < 120 mmHg and Diastolic BP < 80 mmHg.
- Pre-hypertension: Systolic 120-139 mmHg and/or Diastolic 80-89 mmHg. Advise dietary changes, physical activity, and rescreen in 1 year.
- Stage 1 Hypertension: Systolic 140-159 mmHg and/or Diastolic 90-99 mmHg. Refer to Medical Officer for diagnosis and medication. Follow-up visit required every 30 days.
- Stage 2 Hypertension: Systolic >= 160 mmHg and/or Diastolic >= 100 mmHg. Urgent referral to Chandrapuri District Hospital / PHC.
- Hypertensive Emergency: Systolic >= 180 mmHg or Diastolic >= 110 mmHg with severe headache, chest pain, or visual disturbance -> Emergency referral immediately.

### NCD-1.3: Diabetes Mellitus Screening and Blood Sugar Cut-offs
Screening using point-of-care glucometer:
- Random Blood Sugar (RBS):
  - Normal: < 140 mg/dL.
  - Suspected Diabetes: 140 to 199 mg/dL. Refer to PHC for Fasting Blood Sugar (FBS) test.
  - High / Diabetes Range: >= 200 mg/dL accompanied by classic symptoms (polydipsia, polyuria, unexplained weight loss). Refer for confirmation.
- Fasting Blood Sugar (FBS):
  - Normal: 70 to 99 mg/dL.
  - Impaired Fasting Glucose (Pre-diabetes): 100 to 125 mg/dL.
  - Diabetes: >= 126 mg/dL.
- Follow-up: All confirmed diabetic patients require monthly compliance visits and HbA1c testing every 3-6 months.

### NCD-1.4: Medication Adherence, Foot Care, and Lifestyle Counseling
- Medication Adherence: Reiterate that medicines for BP and diabetes must be taken every single day without interruption, even when feeling well.
- Salt Intake: Restrict dietary salt to less than 1 teaspoon (< 5 grams) per day. Avoid papad, pickles, and processed snacks.
- Physical Activity: At least 30 minutes of brisk walking or moderate physical activity 5 days a week.
- Tobacco and Alcohol Cessation: Total cessation of bidi, cigarettes, gutkha, khaini, and alcohol.
- Daily Foot Care for Diabetics: Inspect feet daily for cuts, blisters, redness, or fungal infection; wash and dry between toes; never walk barefoot.

title: Protocol 07: Common Childhood Illnesses Management (CHD)
full_markdown:
# Protocol 07: Common Childhood Illnesses Management (CHD)

Disclaimer: Educational and operational decision support for trained frontline health workers. Protocols are simplified hackathon materials and are not for clinical use. This system does not replace clinical judgment or qualified medical care.

---

### CHD-1.1: Acute Diarrhoea and Dehydration Management
Classification of dehydration:
- No Dehydration: Alert, normal eyes, drinks normally, skin pinch goes back immediately. Manage at home with ORS and extra fluids.
- Some Dehydration: Restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly/thirsty, skin pinch goes back slowly (< 2 seconds). Administer ORS at health sub-centre (approx. 75 ml/kg over 4 hours).
- Severe Dehydration: Lethargic or unconscious, sunken eyes, unable to drink or drinks poorly, skin pinch goes back very slowly (> 2 seconds). Emergency referral for IV fluids (Ringer Lactate) immediately.
- ORS Preparation: Dissolve entire standard packet of Oral Rehydration Salts (20.5g WHO formula) in 1 litre of clean drinking water. Mix well. Use within 24 hours; discard leftover solution after 24 hours.
- Zinc Supplementation: Give daily for 14 continuous days, even after diarrhoea stops:
  - Infants under 6 months: 10 mg elemental zinc per day (half tablet dissolved in expressed breast milk).
  - Children 6 months to 5 years: 20 mg elemental zinc per day (one full tablet dissolved in clean water or breast milk).

### CHD-1.2: Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) and Pneumonia
Fast Breathing Thresholds (count breaths for 1 full minute when child is calm):
- Age < 2 months: 60 breaths per minute or faster.
- Age 2 months to 11 months: 50 breaths per minute or faster.
- Age 12 months to 59 months: 40 breaths per minute or faster.
- Classification and Action:
  - No Pneumonia (Cough/Cold): Normal breathing rate, no chest indrawing. Home care: soothing home fluids (tulsi, ginger, warm water), continue feeding, return immediately if danger signs appear.
  - Pneumonia: Fast breathing, but NO chest indrawing and no general danger signs. Oral antibiotic (Amoxicillin dispersible tablets as per national IMNCI guidelines) prescribed by ANM/MO.
  - Severe Pneumonia: Chest indrawing (lower chest wall moves inward during inspiration) or any general danger sign (stridor, convulsions, inability to drink). Give first dose of antibiotic and REFER IMMEDIATELY to Chandrapuri District Hospital.

### CHD-1.3: Fever and Malaria Screening
- Assess for malaria: In endemic areas, perform Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) for malaria on any child with fever (> 37.5°C / 99.5°F).
- Temperature Management: For high fever (> 38.5°C / 101.3°F), administer Paracetamol syrup/drops (10-15 mg/kg body weight per dose) every 4-6 hours (maximum 4 doses in 24 hours). Perform tepid sponging with normal temperature water; NEVER use ice or cold water.
- Danger signs in fever: Stiff neck, petechial purpuric rash, convulsions, inability to drink, persistent vomiting -> Emergency referral.

title: Protocol 08: Operational Scope, Restrictions, and Redirection Guidance (SCP)
full_markdown:
# Protocol 08: Operational Scope, Restrictions, and Redirection Guidance (SCP)

Disclaimer: Educational and operational decision support for trained frontline health workers. Protocols are simplified hackathon materials and are not for clinical use. This system does not replace clinical judgment or qualified medical care.

---

### SCP-1.1: Out-of-Scope Topics and Clear Boundaries
SwasthyaSaathi is strictly restricted to approved public health workflows for frontline health workers (ASHA/ANM in rural primary care). The system MUST explicitly refuse to answer and redirect when queried about:
1. Prescription-only drug dosages not explicitly specified in standard ASHA/ANM kits (e.g. cardiac medications, intravenous chemotherapy, immunosuppressants, psychiatric drugs, high-dose steroids).
2. Advanced surgical interventions (e.g. caesarean section technique, laparotomy, appendectomy, cosmetic surgery).
3. Complex adult non-communicable diseases outside basic screening (e.g. oncology/cancer staging, dialysis regimens, neurosurgery, rare genetic disorders).
4. Veterinary or animal health questions.
5. Administrative, legal, or non-health inquiries.
6. Autonomous diagnostic assertions ("The patient definitely has appendicitis").

### SCP-1.2: Mandatory Redirection Guidance
When an out-of-scope query is detected:
- The system must set `refused: true` and `escalate: false` (unless a separate danger sign independently requires emergency escalation).
- Output the standardized polite redirection response:
  "Yeh vishay ASHA/ANM ke manak protocol ke daayre se bahar hai. Kripya Chandrapuri District Hospital ya nazdeeki Primary Health Centre (PHC) ke qualified Medical Officer (doctor) se paramarsh lein."
  (Translation: "This topic falls outside the standard protocol scope for ASHA/ANM workers. Please consult the qualified Medical Officer or doctor at Chandrapuri District Hospital or the nearest PHC.")
- Provide no speculative or dangerous diagnostic/dosage advice.

### SCP-1.3: Deterministic Safety Precedence Rule
- Crucial Rule: The emergency danger-sign check ALWAYS executes before the scope guard.
- If a query is outside general protocol scope BUT contains an acute life-threatening symptom or red-flag emergency (e.g. "What antibiotic dose for an unconscious person having continuous fits?" or "Can I give aspirin to a pregnant woman bleeding heavily?"):
  - The deterministic emergency safety engine MUST trigger first!
  - Return `escalate: true`, cite `ESC-1.1` / `ESC-2.1` / etc., and provide immediate referral guidance before any scope refusal.
  - Life-threatening emergencies always take absolute precedence over scope refusal.

title: Protocol 09: Daily Household Visit-List Generation Rules (VIS)
full_markdown:
# Protocol 09: Daily Household Visit-List Generation Rules (VIS)

Disclaimer: Educational and operational decision support for trained frontline health workers. Protocols are simplified hackathon materials and are not for clinical use. This system does not replace clinical judgment or qualified medical care.

---

### VIS-1.1: Planning Scope and Reference Baseline Date
- Target Community: Chandrapuri Block comprising 6 villages (Amrapur, Belwadi Tola, Kesarganj, Dhanpura, Navagaon Khurd, Sitapahari) served by 5 ASHA workers.
- Household Dataset: 500 households, 2,234 registered members.
- Official Development Validation Date: 26 October 2026 (Monday). The household register contains historic event records up to 25 October 2026.
- All date calculations and priority classifications for the benchmark must strictly use 26 October 2026 (`2026-10-26`).

### VIS-1.2: Due-Item Eligibility and Calculation Logic
1. Antenatal Care (ANC) Visits:
   - Calculate gestational age in weeks as of planning date: `(Planning_Date - LMP) / 7`.
   - `ANC_VISIT_1`: 0 to 12 completed weeks. Due if pregnant and no ANC visit recorded yet.
   - `ANC_VISIT_2`: 14 to 26 weeks. Due if pregnant and latest recorded ANC visit was visit 1 (or none).
   - `ANC_VISIT_3`: 28 to 34 weeks. Due if pregnant and latest recorded ANC visit was visit 2 (or fewer).
   - `ANC_VISIT_4`: 36 weeks up to delivery. Due if pregnant and latest ANC visit was visit 3 (or fewer).

2. Tetanus-Diphtheria (Td) Immunisation in Pregnancy:
   - `TD_PREG_1`: Due as soon as pregnancy registered if 0 Td doses recorded.
   - `TD_PREG_2`: Due 4 weeks (28 days) after `TD_PREG_1` if only 1 dose recorded.
   - `TD_BOOSTER`: Due if pregnant woman had 2 doses in a prior pregnancy within last 3 years.

3. High-Risk Pregnancy (HRP) Follow-up:
   - `HRP_FOLLOWUP`: Due every 14 days for any pregnant woman with HRP flag (severe anaemia Hb < 7, BP >= 140/90, age < 18 or > 35, multiple gestation, past C-section) if last visit was >= 14 days ago.

4. Home-Based Newborn Care (HBNC) Visits:
   - Calculate infant age in days: `Planning_Date - Date_of_Birth`.
   - Institutional delivery schedule: Day 3 (`HBNC_D3`), Day 7 (`HBNC_D7`), Day 14 (`HBNC_D14`), Day 21 (`HBNC_D21`), Day 28 (`HBNC_D28`), Day 42 (`HBNC_D42`).
   - Home delivery schedule: Includes Day 1 (`HBNC_D1`) plus Days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, and 42.
   - A visit is due if current age has reached or passed the visit day and that specific visit has not been logged.

5. Childhood Immunisation Doses:
   - At birth (< 15 days): `BCG`, `OPV_0`, `HEP_B_0`.
   - At 6 weeks (42 days): `OPV_1`, `PENTA_1`, `ROTA_1`, `FIPV_1`, `PCV_1`.
   - At 10 weeks (70 days): `OPV_2`, `PENTA_2`, `ROTA_2`.
   - At 14 weeks (98 days): `OPV_3`, `PENTA_3`, `ROTA_3`, `FIPV_2`, `PCV_2`.
   - At 9 months (270 days): `MR_1`, `JE_1`, `PCV_B`, `VIT_A_1`.
   - At 16-24 months (480 days): `MR_2`, `DPT_B1`, `OPV_B`, `VIT_A_2`.
   - At 5-6 years: `DPT_B2`.
   - At 10 years: `TD_10`.
   - At 16 years: `TD_16`.

6. Malnutrition (MUAC) Screening:
   - `MUAC_SCREENING`: Due monthly (every 30 days) for children aged 6 to 59 months previously identified as SAM (MUAC < 11.5 cm) or MAM (MUAC 11.5 - 12.4 cm).
   - Due quarterly (every 90 days) for all other registered children aged 6 to 59 months.

7. Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) Follow-up:
   - `HTN_FOLLOWUP`: Due every 30 days for diagnosed hypertensive individuals (age >= 30).
   - `DM_FOLLOWUP`: Due every 30 days for diagnosed diabetic individuals (age >= 30).

### VIS-1.3: Priority Assignment Rules
Each due visit item MUST be assigned an integer priority:
- Priority 1 (High-Risk and Due/Overdue):
  - Any `HRP_FOLLOWUP` visit.
  - Any infant under 7 days of age requiring HBNC (`HBNC_D1`, `HBNC_D3`, `HBNC_D7`).
  - SAM children due for MUAC screening or follow-up.
  - Overdue visits where the scheduled date is more than 30 days in the past.
  - Hypertensive or diabetic patients overdue for follow-up by more than 14 days.
- Priority 2 (Routine Due / Currently Overdue):
  - Routine ANC visits (`ANC_VISIT_1`, `ANC_VISIT_2`, `ANC_VISIT_3`, `ANC_VISIT_4`) currently due.
  - Routine immunisation doses currently due or overdue by <= 30 days.
  - Routine HBNC visits for Days 14, 21, 28, and 42.
  - Routine NCD monthly follow-ups due.
  - Routine quarterly MUAC screening due.
- Priority 3 (Due This Week / Proactive Window):
  - Any scheduled visit or immunisation becoming due within the next 7 calendar days (26 October 2026 to 1 November 2026 inclusive).

### VIS-1.4: Output Requirements
- File name: `H5_visit_list.csv`
- Header: `member_id,due_item,priority`
- Rows must cover the entire 500-household register.
- Unique combinations of `member_id` and `due_item` only.

  - Any scheduled visit or immunisation becoming due within the next 7 calendar days (26 October 2026 to 1 November 2026 inclusive).

sections.title: Output Requirements
sections.content:
- File name: `H5_visit_list.csv`
- Header: `member_id,due_item,priority`
- Rows must cover the entire 500-household register.
- Unique combinations of `member_id` and `due_item` only.
